blocks: The federal government sued over Zelle scams. Then it dropped the case.
December twentieth, twenty twenty-four. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau sued Zelle's operator and three big banks: JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo.
It alleged that customers complained of fraud losses of more than two hundred million dollars at each of the three banks.
Then, on March fourth, twenty twenty-five, the CFPB dropped it. The judge dismissed the case with prejudice. No court ever ruled on whether the banks did anything wrong.
Five months later, New York's attorney general sued instead, alleging that scammers took more than one billion dollars from Zelle users between twenty seventeen and twenty twenty-three.
Remember, these are allegations. A lawsuit is not a verdict.
The whole story, and how to protect yourself, is on The Rule Changed.
